raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I'm 54, been farming this same patch since I was young. Primary school is all the schooling I got, so I don't bother with the rate tables those young extension fellows bring around. I just do what works.

**My land, how I split it.** I've got 10.1 mu. Six mu I keep in wheat-maize, like always — that's my grain, my family of five eats from that, and what's left I sell. The other four mu and a bit, I plant cotton. Cotton is more work and the price jumps around, but it brings cash in the autumn when we need it. My two oldest do off-farm work in town, so during planting and harvest I can sometimes ask them to come back, but mostly it's me and my wife.

**Wheat (6 mu).** I'll plant around the 10th of October, after the maize comes off. I save some seed from last year's crop, mix it with a bag of bought seed — neighbor said the new variety stands up better to the dry spring. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu before planting, that's about 30 kg, and then around jointing in March I scatter half a bag of urea per mu — maybe 12-13 kg. If it looks yellow I add a bit more. I water before winter (December) for safety, then once at jointing, once at heading. Three waterings is what I usually do — the well costs money to run but if I skip the heading water and it doesn't rain, I lose grain. Spray weeds once in spring. I expect about 400 kg per mu, that's what I usually get. A good year maybe 450.

**Maize (6 mu, after wheat).** Wheat comes off early-mid June, I have to get the maize in within a few days or it's too late. I hire the combine for wheat and the same fellow brings a no-till maize planter — costs me maybe 40-50 yuan per mu but I have no choice, can't do it by hand in time. Hybrid seed, the kind everyone in our village plants now. I put compound fertilizer down with the seed, then topdress urea once at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口期) — maybe 15 kg of urea. Water once or twice depending on the rain. Spray for armyworm if I see them. Yield around 450 kg per mu, sometimes 500 if the rain is right.

**Cotton (4.1 mu).** This is the one that takes the most work. Plant late April, after the soil warms up. I till once with the small tractor I share with my brother. I use one of the standard varieties — not the most expensive seed but not the cheapest either. I put down about two bags of compound at planting, then add urea twice — once before flowering, once during boll-setting, maybe 8-10 kg urea each time. Cotton drinks pesticide — I spray for aphids, bollworm, mites, probably 5-6 times through the summer. That's the biggest expense after fertilizer. Water once or twice if the summer is dry. Picking takes weeks, my wife and I do it ourselves, sometimes my sister-in-law helps. I expect maybe 230 kg of lint per mu — last year was 240, year before only 200 because of the late rain.

**Money.** I keep some cash back for emergencies — never spend everything on inputs. If money runs short I cut the cotton pesticide first because I can see the pests coming and decide then. I won't cut the wheat fertilizer because that's our food.
